def quicksort(arr):
    if len(arr) <= 1:
        return arr
    pivot = arr[len(arr) // 2]
    left = [x for x in arr if x < pivot]
    middle = [x for x in arr if x == pivot]
    right = [x for x in arr if x > pivot]
    return quicksort(left) + middle + quicksort(right)

Here's how merge sort works, step by step.

You take an unsorted list. You split it in half. Then you split each half in half. You keep splitting until every piece is just one element. One element is always sorted.
